capital_project_profiles.title: Bikeshare Program
description_lines: A bikeshare program in Charlottetown to allow residents and visitors to reduce their
reliance on cars and travel throughout the city by bicycle. A selection of electric and
traditional bikes will be offered. An RFP will be issued to select a third-party vendor to
deliver a two-year bikeshare pilot. Depending on bids received, this would include
between 60 and 180 bikes distributed throughout Charlottetown at up to 32 stations for
use by the public.
Community-Building and Placemaking
Governance and Civic Engagement
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Public Transit Buses
description_lines: Diesel buses and electric minibuses to replace aging fleet and deliver on fleet
expansion to allow continued public transit service. Three diesel buses are planned for
delivery in December 2025. Bids for an additional four diesel buses closes in April 2025
for delivery in 2026. In April, planning will begin for four electric minibuses and charging
infrastructure.
Community-Building and Placemaking
Governance and Civic Engagement
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: New Fire Station
description_lines: Finalizing new fire station design, site and pre-construction.
Community-Building and Placemaking
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Fire Engine Replacement
description_lines: Replace three fire engines over the next five years, starting with Engine 4 at Station 2,
that have exceeded their life expectancy as first response vehicles. In accordance with
fire service code and standards, front line vehicles are to be replaced after 20 years of
service. Replacing outdated vehicles will enhance firefighter safety and operational
capabilities required in our growing City.
Community-Building and Placemaking
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: East Royalty Landfill Old Road and Active Transportation Pathway
capital_project_profiles.project: East Royalty Landfill Old Road and Active Transportation Pathway
description_lines: This work will enable the public to access the Parkman Soccer Complex, Acadian Forest
& Trails, East Royalty Park and the neighbourhood of East Royalty from Acadian Drive.
The scope of work includes resurfacing a large section of the old asphalt road,
constructing a gravel driveway for the remaining portion and constructing an Active
Transportation Pathway along the full length of the road and driveway.
Community-Building and Placemaking
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Artificial Turf Field
description_lines: Complete design and drawings and cost estimate for one artificial turf field that can be
used from April to November every year for up to 2,500 hours of use per season.
Construction is expected to start by September 2025.
Community-Building and Placemaking
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Multi-Use Outdoor Facility
description_lines: The outdoor sports facility located in the Elmer MacFadyen Memorial Recreational
Complex is at the end of its life; the city is unable to maintain the facility as an
aesthetically pleasing venue and to maintain safety standards.
A new outdoor facility will include a permanent artificial ice making system with a chiller
unit, new boards, lighting and playing surface. Ice-making has become very difficult
due to changing weather conditions. A permanent ice-making system will allow for the
facility to maintain ice longer in the season, weather permitting. The city will engage
with the public and keep them up to date on the new and improved multi-use facility
that will be functional in all four seasons.
Community-Building and Placemaking
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Heartz Hall Upgrades â€“ Phase 2
description_lines: The historic Heartz Hall building was relocated on its original property in 2024 due to
the widening of St. Peters Rd. Phase 2 activities involve interior work and appropriate
modernizations.
Community-Building and Placemaking
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Sherwood Recreation Hall Upgrades
description_lines: The Sherwood Recreation Hall is an ageing building that needs to be assessed for
future services. Funding will be used to generate reports that consider options including
renovations, reconstruction and alignment with adjacent services. This work may
progress to some preparatory work for an approved future vision for the Hall.
Community-Building and Placemaking
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Brownfield Development
description_lines: Funding for the 2025/26 fiscal year will involve the potential acquisition and upgrades
of environmentally sensitive properties. Negotiations are not yet complete.
Community-Building and Placemaking
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Pownal Street Parkade
description_lines: The Pownal Street Parkade was built in 1986, and the structure is in need of significant
renovation work to maintain its integrity. Work will include the replacement of rebar and
concrete.
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Queen Street Parkade Upgrades
description_lines: The Queen Street Parkade was constructed in 1979 and has undergone major
maintenance over its lifecycle. The building is now in need of significant renovation work
to ensure structural integrity.
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Parks and Recreation Small Fleet Replacement
capital_project_profiles.project: Parks and Recreation Small Fleet Replacement
description_lines: Parks and Recreation Small Fleet Replacement for the 2025/26 fiscal year includes a
Salt Hopper, V-Plow attachment, 4 work truck replacements, an additional 1/2 ton
truck, an additional 21' trailer and 2 new 72" mowers.
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Public Works Small Fleet Replacement
capital_project_profiles.project: Parks and Recreation Small Fleet Replacement
description_lines: Public Works Small Fleet Replacement for the 2025/26 fiscal year includes ten 1/2 ton
trucks, four 3/4 ton trucks, and four 1-ton trucks.
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Public Works Large Fleet Replacement
description_lines: 3 plow trucks were ordered last year and are expected to be delivered in the 2025-26
fiscal year at a total cost of $1.25 million. Large Fleet Replacement for Public Works also
includes the purchase of 3 sidewalk machines and a new aerial chipper for the
Environment and Sustainability Department for a total $1.21 million.
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Construction of New Sidewalks
description_lines: New sidewalk construction in the 2025/26 fiscal year includes new infill sidewalk and
paved paths in developed areas. Three sections awarded in 2024 are expected to be
completed in the following areas: 375m on Angus Dr., 80m on Birch Hill Dr., 450m on
Montgomery Dr.
2025 plans also include 275m on Eleana Crt., 175m on Elizabeth St., 400m on Parkside Dr.
as well as the design of 560m on Westcomb Cres. and 750m on Stockman Dr.
Inclusive Economic Growth

capital_project_profiles.title: Street Resurfacing
description_lines: This is an annual paving program focused on a worst-first approach while still giving
consideration to efficient coordination with other upcoming and anticipated projects.
At current costs, this reflects 4 per cent of inventory which is a 25-year return cycle.
Inclusive Economic Growth
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Exhibition Drive Reconstruction
description_lines: The wastewater storm system on Exhibition Drive is currently end-of-life and is
experiencing issues that require replacement. Staff are currently assessing coordination
with pedestrian and active transport plans.
Inclusive Economic Growth
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: New Traffic Lights
description_lines: This work will involve the replacement of traffic signals with upgraded technology and
hardware. The focus for the 2025/26 fiscal year will be on the Grafton Street corridor
which includes Weymouth, Prince and Queen Streets.
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Wellfield Protection
description_lines: This project proposes purchasing land within wellfield protection zones. Expanding the
City’s possession of land by wellfield protection zones will increase the municipality’s
ability to continue protecting its award winning groundwater quality and enhance
natural areas.
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Water Distribution System Upgrades
description_lines: Water distribution system upgrades and ageing infrastructure renewals.
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Collector Sewer Liftstations Rehabilitation
description_lines: Replacement of obsolete liftstation equipment, which will minimize downtime and
increase resiliency and capacity. This project includes upgrades to the Charlottetown
collector sewer liftstations, replacement of pumps, electronic controllers and monitoring
equipment.
Infrastructure and the Environment

capital_project_profiles.title: Aeration Tank Rehabilitation
description_lines: Aeration Tank Rehabilitation at the Charlottetown Pollution Control Plant which includes
replacement and enhancement of wastewater aeration basin components at the
Charlottetown Pollution Control Plant, minimizing process downtime and increasing
resiliency.
Infrastructure and the Environment
